segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, um.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Is everybody, yeah, I think we can start.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So, uh, welcome to the kickoff meeting for the new project.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, first thing, Priya can't make it today, she's at the supplier visit in, uh, in Eindhoven.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Oh, is that the whole day?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Whole day, yeah. So it's just the three of us.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, so I'm Helen, I'll be the project manager on this one.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Uh, do you want to just quickly say who you are and what you do?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, sure. Um, I'm Tomasz, I'm the marketing expert.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So I'll be looking at, uh, what the users want, what the market looks like, that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And I'm Kofi, user interface designer.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: So basically everything the user touches and sees on the, on the screen.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And Priya's our industrial designer, so she'll do the, um, the physical side, the casing and the components.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, so the project.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Uh, we're designing a self-checkout kiosk for libraries.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So a stand-alone unit where people can, um, borrow and return books themselves without going to the desk.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Public libraries, or like university libraries as well?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, the brief says mainly public libraries. Medium-sized branch libraries.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And the idea is it should be, uh, original, trendy and user-friendly. That's the phrase they used.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Trendy library kiosk. Right.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, I know. Um.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So the way we'll work is three, well, four meetings. This one, then functional design, conceptual design, and detailed design.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And in between you each work on your own part and bring it back.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, before we get into it, quick icebreaker.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Everyone say the, uh, the last book you actually took out of a library.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Oh, the last...

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Uh, honestly, I think it was a cookbook. A couple of years ago.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mine was a travel guide for Portugal. Which I returned late.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Ha.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So I've paid my fine, I've seen how the desk works.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's actually useful for this.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: It is, yeah. Okay, mine was a crime novel, but anyway.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, so the money side.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: We're supposed to sell the kiosk at three and a half thousand euros per unit to the library networks.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And the production cost can't be more than fourteen hundred euros a unit.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Fourteen hundred including the screen?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Including everything. Screen, scanner, casing, the lot.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, that's, that's tight-ish.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: And what's the, um, the target number? How many are they hoping to sell?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: They want, uh, to sell around four thousand units in the first two years.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So, um, first ideas. Anything that comes to mind.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Well, from the library side, the big thing is the queues at the desk.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Especially Saturday mornings, families with like twenty picture books.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So it has to handle a stack of books, not one at a time.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That kind of points to RFID, right? Where you just put the whole pile on a pad.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, exactly.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Do most libraries have RFID tags in their books already?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um, a lot do, but not all. Some of the smaller ones are still on barcodes.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And then you'd need a barcode scanner as well.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Hmm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Which costs more, and it's another, another thing for the user to figure out.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: But if we only do RFID we cut out part of the market.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, true.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: That's probably a question for Priya as well, the component cost.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, and on the screen side, um, I'm thinking we keep it really simple.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Like, card in, books on the pad, done. Three steps.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And actually, um, we're going touchscreen only. No keypad, no physical buttons at all. That's decided.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Uh.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: What about, um, people typing in their PIN?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: On-screen keypad.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, um.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Let's, let's not go too deep into the screen yet, that's more next meeting.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Tomasz, anything else from the user side?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um, yeah, accessibility.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Libraries get a lot of older users, and also kids, and wheelchair users.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So the height of the thing matters, and the, the size of text.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: That's a good point, yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: And they'll probably want it to match the library's branding, the colours and the logo.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Maybe a removable front panel or something they can print on.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: That could be nice, yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Again that's Priya's area, but put it on the list.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, so, um, the jobs for next meeting.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Priya, since she's not here, I'll give her the working design.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So she should look at the hardware components. Scanner versus RFID pad, the screen, the casing, and what they cost against the fourteen hundred.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Will you tell her or should one of us?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I'll email her this afternoon with the notes.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Kofi, you've got the technical functions design.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So what the kiosk actually needs to do, the, uh, the steps the user goes through.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: I'll sketch out the borrow and the return flow.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And Tomasz, user requirements.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So like what library users actually want from it?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, users, and also the library staff, what they need from it.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I could, um, I could ask the branch on Wilson Street, they're always happy to chat.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Perfect, yeah, do that.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: And I'll also see what the competitors are charging, just roughly.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay. Everyone clear?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Sorry, and the touchscreen thing, so are we...

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, we'll come back to that next time when we've all got our bits.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, I'd want to hear from the library people first.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay, fair.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Right. So, uh, recap. Priya, working design, I'll email her.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Kofi, technical functions. Tomasz, user requirements.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And I'll send out the minutes.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Next meeting is in, uh, thirty minutes, so grab a coffee.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Thanks, Helen.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, thanks everyone.

abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, noted that the industrial designer was absent because of a supplier visit, and had the marketing expert and user interface designer introduce themselves.

The project manager presented the brief: a stand-alone self-checkout kiosk for medium-sized public libraries, to be original, trendy and user-friendly, sold at 3,500 euros per unit with a maximum production cost of 1,400 euros and a target of about 4,000 units in two years.

The team discussed first ideas: the marketing expert stressed desk queues and the need to process a stack of books at once, which the user interface designer linked to RFID, although some libraries still use barcodes.
The marketing expert raised accessibility for older users, children and wheelchair users, and the idea of matching library branding, possibly with a removable printable front panel.
The user interface designer declared the kiosk would be touchscreen only, but this was questioned and the project manager deferred it to the next meeting.
The project manager closed by assigning individual tasks for the functional design meeting, including the working design for the absent industrial designer.
actions: The industrial designer (absent) is to work on the working design: hardware components such as barcode scanner versus RFID pad, screen and casing, costed against the 1,400 euro limit.
The project manager will email the industrial designer the notes and her assignment.
The user interface designer will do the technical functions design, sketching the borrow and return flows.
The marketing expert will research user requirements from library users and staff, including talking to the Wilson Street branch, and roughly check competitor pricing.
The project manager will send out the minutes.
decisions: The kiosk must be able to process a stack of books at once rather than one book at a time.
Accessibility (kiosk height, text size, suitability for older users, children and wheelchair users) will be treated as a requirement.
problems: Whether to support RFID only or also include a barcode scanner is unresolved; RFID-only would exclude libraries still using barcodes, while adding a scanner raises cost and complexity.
The user interface designer's claim that the kiosk will be touchscreen only with no physical buttons was not agreed and was deferred to the next meeting.
The 1,400 euro production cost limit, including screen, scanner and casing, is considered tight.

action_items.description: Working design: investigate hardware components (barcode scanner vs RFID pad, screen, casing, possible removable front panel) and their cost against the 1,400 euro limit
Email the absent industrial designer the meeting notes and her assignment
Technical functions design: define what the kiosk must do and sketch the borrow and return flows
User requirements: find out what library users and staff need, including talking to the Wilson Street branch
Roughly check what competitors charge for library self-checkout kiosks
